# agent-spaces — Active Invariants

## acp.jobs.node-execution-ownership

Agent profiles may declare jobs.default_node and schedules may override it with execution.node. Each accepts one logical HRC node ID, a non-empty list, or the reserved all wildcard. Compilation emits canonical desiredJson.execution.nodes: concrete members are validated, deduplicated, and sorted; all remains exactly ["all"]; local and all mixed with concrete members are rejected. The owner set authorizes deliberate independent per-node fan-out in ACP and is never a source for a JobRun's singular execution identity. This contract is separate from HRC scope placement.

## agent-spaces.agent-harness-runtime-boundary

Amendment T-08680 (2026-09-21, corrected and ruled by Lance) preserves the agent-harness-tmux child topology while retiring only its private protocol. The agent-harness and agent-harness-tmux driver identities are served by one identity-bound agent-harness executable in an immutable ASP release. ASPC interprets the mutable agent declaration and emits a complete hash-covered broker profile. aspd selects only an inspected binding and freezes the exact release worker in executionRelease.worker.executable; both bindings name that executable and hostedDrivers is positive evidence derived from the release binding table. HRC launches that worker generically and retains placement, terminal-lease, lifecycle, routing, and durable-messaging authority, but it does not build an agent-harness plan, register either driver, import the first-party runtime, infer a worker, or speak an agent-harness-private protocol. Both profiles use the native-worker process alternative: no process command or arguments exist and harnessTransport is native-worker, meaning the already-external release worker directly owns the selected runtime and speaks the standard harness-broker protocol. Native-worker is distinct from HRC-local in-process execution. Headless selects agent-harness with no terminal and owns the Pi runtime in the worker. Interactive selects agent-harness-tmux: HRC launches the outer release worker generically and supplies a tmux pane lease; the registered driver consumes that lease and launches the same release executable as a TUI child in the pane. A worker-local Unix socket carries the standard harness-broker protocol directly between them. The child registers the leaf agent-harness-tmux driver, owns Pi and InteractiveMode, and is the sole mapper for Pi events. The outer driver verifies broker.hello and exact release identity, invokes the standard invocation methods, and re-sequences child envelopes into its real DriverContext. No agent-harness-control/v1, session-config, turn-begin, or other private wire contract exists. Both drivers require the semantic agent block and a Pi SDK model binding, while the outer runtime discriminator remains the distinct first-party agent-harness value. The shared Pi driver owns auth, permission, continuation, mapping, interruption, and disposal in the child; its presentation observes operator turns in that same mapper. Earendil InteractiveMode process exit is confined to the child and can never terminate the outer release worker. The direct runtime continues to use AgentSpacesResourceLoader as its sole resource-delivery boundary. It resolves ordered ASP sources and contextual prompt, reminder, skills, model, auth, permission, and environment without a harness adapter, compiler-built merged Pi bundle, ambient Pi discovery, or generated external-harness home; every replacement session reloads that boundary. Foreground asp run remains a separate local TUI/print surface using the same runtime factory. Existing external-harness, generic Pi SDK, Arris, Muse, and Desktop routes retain their own contracts, and HRC retains all non-execution semantic authority named by their active records.

## agent-spaces.agent-inspection-authority

Agent Spaces is the sole authority for canonical agent roster discovery and contextual inspection assembly. Its consumer-facing catalog and inspection operations accept only validated agent and project identifiers plus declared inspection overrides; filesystem paths, roots, environment snapshots, clocks, probe results, scaffolds, and compile options never cross that boundary. Agent Spaces resolves trusted project placement, current producer sources, and runtime context internally, validates a requested agent against that freshly resolved context, and returns only the shared public DTO. A project-neutral catalog never invents a project or emits project-contextual compile options, and lower-level context-taking primitives remain internal to the producer boundary for external consumers. The separately named resolveRuntimeDeclaration and inspectRuntimePlacement preparation operations are governed by agent-spaces.runtime-declaration-authority and accept only their exact placement context DTOs; they do not add paths, roots, environment, or placement inputs to identifier-only catalogAgentInspection or inspectAgentSelection.

## agent-spaces.aspd-release-worker-hosting

Amendment T-08680 (2026-09-21, ruled by Lance): the identity-bound agent-harness release executable binds both agent-harness and agent-harness-tmux and directly serves the standard broker protocol. It is a native worker, not the deferred generic Pi SDK binding described in the named gap below. Release inspection must prove its hermetic closure, embedded identity, dual driver inventory, explicit dual bindings, and positive hostedDrivers before either route is exposed. Subject to that amendment, A binding-aware standalone ASP release declares each release-supported broker driver's worker executable and each required ASP-owned asset in its immutable release manifest. Inspection proves every declared worker is identity-bound, resolves inside that release, advertises every driver bound to it, and matches its recorded digests. That release's compiled aspd selects a worker only through the declared binding, freezes the selected executable in the existing per-preparation executionRelease.worker.executable, and emits optional executionRelease.worker.hostedDrivers as the sorted set of manifest bindings assigned to that executable. hostedDrivers is positive hosting evidence, not an inference from extra registered drivers; a missing selected-driver binding returns release_worker_driver_unavailable on the existing compile failure envelope before executionRelease or any hosting effect. ASP-owned Claude and Pi hook and tmux helpers execute through the selected release payload, and the verified Claude statusline asset is copied into the materialized bundle so no durable helper reference depends on PATH, import.meta, a checkout, or a retired release. Retained pre-binding v1 releases remain valid immutable rollback targets with their own compiled behavior and may omit both binding metadata and hostedDrivers; absence is not positive non-Codex hosting evidence. Consumers may preserve the proven legacy codex-app-server binding, but any non-Codex aspd launch admitted on release hosting evidence must require hostedDrivers to contain the selected broker driver. HRC retains worker hosting, lifecycle, placement, and routing authority, except the participant-owned codex-desktop broker (T-08594, 2026-09-17, ruled by Lance, recorded hrc-runtime T-08567 C-23749): hook-started from the active release and served in-process, never HRC-hosted.

## agent-spaces.codex-tui-app-server-presentation

Interactive Codex compatibility seats compile to the codex-app-server driver with codex-tui presentation and websocket-over-unix transport while headless codex-app-server seats and their tmux-tui renderer retain existing initial-turn behavior. Both presentations use native steering confirmation under agent-spaces.harness-broker-turn-evidence: turn/steer carries the pending client identity, and only its matching committed native user item confirms context entry without replacing initiating ownership. The transcript landing evidence enum denotes asynchronous provider evidence here; nativeSourceKind remains provider-jsonrpc. Each interactive runtime owns exactly one app-server started beneath the HRC-leased tmux pane wrapper; pane exit or teardown kills that server, so neither server nor its queued work can outlive the runtime that owns its broker. The broker initializes and subscribes first with the experimental API enabled; the stock remote Codex TUI attaches as the second client after thread start or resume. The driver advertises steer and queue only. Launch and later obligation-bearing inputs enter the same broker-held FIFO and one head at a time reaches Codex via thread/queue/add with clientUserMessageId; turn/start is never sent and exclusive is unsupported. Resume scrubs every durable Codex queue item before loading the thread, and a runtime crash has at-least-once delivery semantics with the old submission failed and any resend carrying fresh identity. The RPC notification stream is the sole turn evidence authority. Observed brackets and attribution obey agent-spaces.harness-broker-turn-evidence, including fail-closed unknown attribution before an item. Approval policy is exactly never in this presentation. Stop and PostToolUse hooks are raw provenance and synchronous mail-stop control only; they mint no turn events. codex-cli-tmux is deprecated in place until a separate removal ruling.

## agent-spaces.harness-broker-admission

One harness-broker owns one harness process and exposes per-seat mechanism; HRC permanently owns cross-seat scheduling and caller policy. Every mediated submission enters exactly one admission class: steer enters the harness-local queue seeking absorption and may instead execute after drain; queue remains broker-held FIFO until idle and then originates its own turn; exclusive originates a turn only when immediately idle or rejects busy; preempt is authority-gated, interrupts the live turn and every drain-spawned successor until true quiescence, then injects the held submission as its own turn while recording any fast completion honestly. Every submission has stable identity, exactly one authoritative disposition, and a turn manifest mapping each turn to the submissions it carried. If a codex-cli-tmux own-turn delivery reaches a contested turn terminal without truthful content correlation, the broker records submission.lost with execution explicitly indeterminate, then records a non-retryable invocation.failed before any later same-seat delivery; HRC owns failed-run projection and fresh-runtime provisioning. A codex-tui codex-app-server seat advertises steer and queue only: launch and later queue submissions remain in the broker-held FIFO until idle, and one head at a time reaches Codex's idle-only queue with its broker input identity. A foreign human or autonomous turn never contests that pending delivery. If an observed turn terminalizes before any item supplies ownership evidence, the turn is unknown; it contests the pending delivery and records the same indeterminate submission.lost then non-retryable invocation.failed boundary before another same-seat input can drain. Obligation-bearing submissions use only queue, exclusive, or preempt and originate a dedicated turn; steer carries no obligation, wait, or own response and resolves only through absorbed or executed disposition. Admission composes driver capability, active-turn policy, and caller authority without silent class upgrades. The broker-held queue is queryable, cancellable, TTL-aware, and reorderable under authority; admission queue disposition interrupt and capture decisions share the broker replay ledger and snapshot surface. TUI mechanics never use navigation-key choreography, and unsupported capabilities remain unset. Turn evidence and bracket-minting declarations remain governed by agent-spaces.harness-broker-turn-evidence and its bounded Pi accepted risk.

## agent-spaces.harness-broker-local-commit-observation

The harness-broker commits execution facts locally and publishes only committed normalized broker envelopes. Provider authority is declared per event family: native transcripts or notification streams own families they represent completely, while hooks remain discovery, wakeup, synchronous control, and missing-evidence inputs. Every provider input is committed verbatim with a source epoch, cursor, and provenance before the same production normalizer handles live delivery or replay; every raw row reaches one durable normalized, state-only, duplicate, ignored-known, or blocked-unknown disposition. In codex-tui observed mode, a committed native turn-start row opens the bracket without borrowing pending input identity; the first committed item row attributes ownership, and a terminal reached before any item attributes unknown solely from committed row order. No live queue query participates, so live ingest and replay produce the same attribution, terminal ordering, and row disposition. An unclassified type, including a load-bearing one and a queue operation used for turn attribution, warns loudly and advances its normalization cursor: it records the blocked-unknown disposition, commits a capture warning, and writes one rate-limited WARN line on the broker's own log, never holding later records. A normalized append failure prevents publication. The bounded Pi risk remains exactly the exception governed by agent-spaces.harness-broker-turn-evidence: the manager-authored delivery-asserted turn.started owns the initial bracket, hooks correlate provider evidence into that bracket without reminting it, and Pi session JSONL is non-authoritative until a separately approved evidence change. The stable replay-follow observer socket is read-only, bounded, and carries no mutation or acknowledgement method. An immutable release may also expose its private retained ledger through the one-shot release-owned offline evidence reader. That reader returns only already-committed normalized envelopes, reports authoritative retention floor and torn/corrupt/unstable snapshot conditions, and never normalizes pending raw rows, repairs evidence, follows a live file, acknowledges, prunes, starts a worker, or acquires a retention claim. HRC is the sole retention-bearing consumer and advances one durable scalar acknowledgement per invocation only through its fenced control connection; other observers accept the retained floor. All mutating RPCs remain on that fenced connection. Explicit permission decisions are HRC-owned, while a disconnected deadline fallback is broker-owned and may release the provider only after permission.resolved is durably committed; failure to commit keeps the provider gate closed.

## agent-spaces.harness-broker-turn-evidence

Amendment T-08680 (2026-09-21, ruled by Lance): agent-harness-tmux is worker-native and no longer uses delivery acknowledgement through a private turn.begin handshake. Its outer driver sends standard invocation.input to a standard broker endpoint in the TUI child. The child broker acknowledgement supplies the turn identity; the outer broker owns the HRC-facing delivered bracket, while operator input is mapped once by the child and relayed without an input id. The agent-harness runtime-boundary record owns the process and attribution law. All private agent-harness turn.begin clauses formerly in this record are superseded. Subject to that amendment, Except for the bounded legacy risk recorded as agent-spaces.pi-delivery-asserted-turn-start, harness-broker turn lifecycle brackets are minted only at the evidence moment declared by the driver: delivery-acknowledged drivers may open a bracket after an answered harness handshake, while harness-evidence drivers open one only from a hook or transcript observation. Observed drivers open from a committed native turn start before ownership is known and attribute separately from the first item: only a user item carrying a pending broker client id is own, null or unknown client ids are foreign human input, and a non-user first item is foreign autonomous input. A terminal before any item attributes unknown. Identity on every turn-scoped event flows only from own attribution; foreign and unknown terminals never borrow a pending input id. Unknown attribution contests a pending delivery and its terminal records indeterminate submission.lost then non-retryable invocation.failed, while foreign attribution never contests. The declaration is advertised per driver and gates the shared delivery-time synthesis. codex-cli-tmux remains harness-evidence: state at the driver/manager boundary may attach a pending broker input to an input-ID-less native UserPromptSubmit only when exact or otherwise unambiguous prompt-content evidence matches; priming and different operator prompts remain unowned, and turn order never lends identity. An unmatched contested terminal records indeterminate submission.lost followed by non-retryable invocation.failed, so no later input drains into that invocation. claude-code-tmux is harness-evidence: an overlapping prompt is buffered without a user.message until strict-order harness evidence resolves it. A remove row alone resolves nothing; hook-driven transcript rows are consumed before the triggering hook's own effects, and correlated remove and queued_command rows join the then-live turn through submission.absorbed, including batched remove-and-attachment sequences. Unresolved removal evidence warns and remains pending rather than minting a terminal disposition. Dequeue only marks a prompt drain-pending, the later plain user row opens an executed turn, and an interrupt marker terminalizes the still-active original turn. Each tracked prompt produces exactly one disposition and at most one user.message; absorption never fabricates a new turn bracket. For Claude, releasing a contested admission slot does not settle the pending input: an unrelated turn terminal or elapsed time cannot cancel, lose, or erase its native correlation or authorize reinjection. Correlated native evidence settles it once, without a last-wins disposition override. The additive optional input.rejected.deliveryEvidence field distinguishes not_written from possibly_written; omission and untyped driver failures convey uncertainty, never a no-write guarantee. Only a refusal before any body write attempt may claim not_written. Once paste or send-keys begins, failures including paste-to-Enter and after-submit failures are possibly_written. A possibly-written Claude failure retains the pending correlation and undisposed submission, emits diagnostic input.rejected, and cannot emit terminal submission.rejected merely because the write operation threw; later native evidence may still report consumption. Proven no-write refusal, native recall, and definitive teardown retain their truthful outcomes. Teardown ends process-local tracking and proves no native removal; this repair establishes no live reattach or restart reconstruction. An evidenced Claude start naming a pending input selects that exact identity before any ordering fallback, regardless of age or allocated turn-number order. Provider queue evidence may establish FIFO among identical bodies; multiple unclassified identical candidates without identity or order evidence remain unresolved with a diagnostic, never selected by oldest or newest age. Full-body contains attribution must also be unambiguous. Ambiguity preserves candidate correlations until native settlement, confirmed recall, or teardown. Codex app-server steering, in TUI and headless modes, confirms context entry only from a committed item/started userMessage whose clientId matches a pending steer and whose threadId and turnId match the identities snapshotted before the RPC. Correlation is armed before sending clientUserMessageId with expectedTurnId. The observer examines every user item and deduplicates by thread, turn, and item identity; item/completed is not a second landing. A match emits native-provenance user.message then submission.absorbed for that exact input and turn once. It never establishes initiating attribution, replaces currentInputId or the turn owner, or resolves a queue-initiator waiter. Unmatched later human items remain visible without broker input identity; headless initial-message behavior remains free of duplicate native rows. RPC success reports input.accepted only. The shared manager never synthesizes submission.absorbed from ack, asserted, or null landing evidence, and the Codex driver never fabricates a broker.steer user.message on acknowledgement. Legacy asserted and Pi SDK ack steering remain available at their declared strength without inferred confirmation; agent-harness false/null stays intact. A matching native item before the RPC response wins: a later response conflict is diagnostic and neither retracts the disposition nor fails an otherwise live invocation solely to dispose the input. Before native evidence, a mismatched or failed RPC response, or the armed target turn terminalizing before the response arrives, always asks the shared manager to start an own turn with the same submission. The fallback retains possibly_written evidence: it is an explicit at-least-once policy that accepts duplicate delivery rather than a silent steer loss. Only a documented pre-write rejection guarantee permits not_written. Tool gaps and unrelated items infer no absorption. A target terminal or interrupt without an exact native match retires the steer correlation and starts the fallback; a late original-turn user item remains visible conversation evidence but cannot replace the fallback's authoritative executed disposition. Definitive teardown or withdrawal remains terminal and later conversation evidence cannot reopen it. Controller reconnect preserves correlation only while the armed target remains live; committed replay uses the same idempotent observer. Driver disposal clears process-local tracking and establishes no process-persistent reconstruction. A provider missing clientId retains native-only confirmation but takes the same fail-open fallback at the target terminal. Shared inference removal and native emission ship coherently; Codex reinjection is deliberately authorized only by this fail-open boundary.

## agent-spaces.portable-immutable-source

A generated portable ASP lock records immutable space source authority only as repository identity plus canonical remote. ## agent-spaces.runtime-declaration-authority

Agent Spaces alone interprets mutable agent profiles, project targets, provisioning overlays, priming, harness/provider/frontend mappings, prompt composition, node-local harness capability, and historical continuation artifact format. HRC supplies its already-decided placement context and keeps project registry, task-worktree selection, home-node placement, authorization, continuation selection, launch, attachment, and lifecycle authority. resolveRuntimeDeclaration and inspectRuntimePlacement re-read applicable sources on every request; an exact caller agentRoot is read without roster search or substitution, project mode none reads no marker or target, and caller agent-source configuration is canonicalized, echoed, and never silently replaced by daemon configuration. Runtime-placement inspection, direct preparation, and launch preparation project one ASP-owned preparation execution context. Template exec, predicate, and interpolation evaluation use the aspd ambient environment plus producer-derived placement correlation; dispatchEnv remains launch-process and dispatch input only and never enters that prompt environment or its canonical hash. Inspection correlation is an additive input behind the exact inspectRuntimePlacementPreparationCorrelation capability; a consumer that requires parity fails closed when the capability is absent rather than presenting an uncorrelated inspection. Explicit prompt-source authority is exclusive: compile uses request aspHome, context surfaces use validated caller agentSources, and ambient home and roots apply only when that surface has no explicit source; explicit and ambient source arms are never merged. A sessionRef identity that contradicts explicit context identity is refused as configured_context_mismatch. Declaration absent and invalid remain distinct from producer unavailable and protocol/context incompatible. observeRuntimeCapability performs only bounded read-only detection and never reports a failed, timed-out, or over-limit probe as positive capability. observeContinuationArtifact uses key-bound frozen provider-home evidence for positive missing; unbound recorded placement may prove presence but absence remains unknown/home_not_historical. No unusable continuation silently starts fresh. Four additive preparation operations keep direct process invocation and Desktop identity, new-registration admission, and fresh-observer preparation under ASP authority without starting a native command or applying input. Direct preparation preserves the placement builder result and carries mandatory structured prompt content. Desktop identity remains separate from admission; existing registrations and durable reattach require no fresh preparation, and the native Desktop lifecycle stays external. The thin ASPC protocol/client closure carries DTOs, validation, framing, and transport only, never configuration, compiler, adapter, or provider implementations.
